Posted October 8, 2007
Analysis by Richard Cowan

In what seems like a sub-plot to a TV crime drama (CSI = Cannabis Scene Investigation?), a Jacksonville University football player, Cecil Coltrane, has admitted that he planted more than 20 grams of marijuana in a teammate's room to so that he could take his place on the team.

See LA Times: Player planted pot in teammate's room

According to the AP, Small was arrested after the Jacksonville police had acted on a tip and searched his dorm room. Of course, the University immediately suspended the victim, and he was not allowed to play in the next game, but it is not clear just why the police could search his room on an anonymous tip.

"The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures, shall not be violated, and no warrants shall issue but upon probable cause, supported by oath or affirmation, and particularly describing the place to be searched, and the person or things to be seized." -- The Fourth Amendment to the Constitution of the United States in the Bill of Rights.)

In any case, it is immediately obvious to anyone that the envious player did something morally (and legally) reprehensible. Now he has been suspended and will face some sort of criminal charges.

The fact that he planted a problematic term for placing the flowers of a plant more than 20 grams means that he knew that possession of that much is a felony in Florida, which could get his victim up to 5 years in prison, but more likely just ruin his life.

Talk about missing the point!
